title: Trentino-Alto Adige's Methane Premium Is Quietly Shrinking
dek: Petrol and diesel keep climbing in lockstep with the national market, but the region's historically expensive natural gas is losing its edge as prices catch up everywhere else.
executive_summary: As of September 16, drivers in Trentino-Alto Adige paid €2.1872/L for self-service Benzina, €2.3068/L for Gasolio, €0.8024/L for GPL and €1.966/L for Metano — all four fuels above the national self-service average that day, with petrol and diesel up roughly six-tenths of a cent from the day before and GPL and Metano essentially flat. Across the region's 392 registered stations, 372 reported prices, a 94.9% reporting rate that beats the national average of 90.2% and edged up by one more station than the previous day.

The daily numbers only tell half the story. Pulled back to the nine tracked weeks since July 20, Benzina and Gasolio in Trentino-Alto Adige have risen almost exactly in step with the national market — up 7.6% and 3.9% regionally versus 7.9% and 3.9% nationally. GPL and Metano are where the region is genuinely diverging: local LPG has crept up 1.4% while the national LPG average has actually slipped slightly, and — the standout finding this week — Trentino-Alto Adige's usually steep Metano premium over the rest of Italy has narrowed by more than a third since late July, as national methane prices surge faster than the region's own.

fuel_sections.heading: Petrol Extends Its Nine-Week Climb, Still a Premium Pump
paragraphs: Self-service Benzina in Trentino-Alto Adige closed at €2.1872/L on September 16, up €0.0132 (+0.61%) from €2.1740/L the day before. That puts the region 2.04% above the national self-service average of €2.1435/L on the same day — a gap that has held fairly steady through the recent run-up, meaning local pumps aren't pulling further away from the rest of the country, just riding the same wave a little higher.

Zooming out to the full nine-week window, regional Benzina has climbed from €2.0210/L in the week of July 20 (W30) to €2.1747/L in the week of September 14 (W38) — a 7.6% increase. Nationally, the same period saw self-service petrol rise 7.9%, from €1.9756/L to €2.1309/L. The two curves are close enough to call this a genuinely national trend rather than a regional story: petrol has been getting steadily more expensive everywhere since late summer, and Trentino-Alto Adige is simply tracking it, week for week, without much local distortion.

fuel_sections.heading: Diesel's Steady Summer Climb Mirrors the National Curve Almost Exactly
paragraphs: Diesel in the region reached €2.3068/L self-service on September 16, up €0.0140 (+0.61%) day-over-day from €2.2928/L, and 1.50% above the national self-service figure of €2.2728/L for the same date. Like petrol, that premium over the national average has stayed narrow and stable rather than widening — Trentino-Alto Adige diesel is expensive relative to the rest of Italy, but not becoming more so.

Over the nine tracked weeks, regional Gasolio rose from €2.2063/L (W30) to €2.2927/L (W38), a 3.9% increase, against a near-identical 3.85% national rise from €2.1747/L to €2.2585/L over the same stretch. Diesel is the fuel where region and nation move most in sync this year: the weekly series barely diverges at any point between July and September, suggesting diesel pricing here is driven almost entirely by the same wholesale and refining pressures affecting the whole country, with no meaningful local premium expansion to flag.

fuel_sections.heading: LPG Holds Nearly Flat Locally While the National Average Quietly Slips
paragraphs: GPL edged up to €0.8024/L self-service on September 16, a modest €0.0020 (+0.25%) gain from €0.8004/L the previous day. That leaves it 6.22% above the national self-service average of €0.7554/L — proportionally the widest gap of any of the four fuels, even though LPG remains by far the cheapest option at the pump in absolute terms.

The multi-week picture is where GPL gets interesting: regional LPG rose 1.4% over the nine weeks tracked, from €0.7912/L (W30) to €0.8024/L (W38), while the national LPG average actually fell 0.6%, from €0.7592/L to €0.7547/L, over the identical period. That's the only fuel of the four where region and nation moved in opposite directions — Trentino-Alto Adige's LPG got a little more expensive at the same time the rest of Italy's got a little cheaper, quietly widening what was already the largest proportional regional premium in the dataset.

fuel_sections.heading: The Region's Big Methane Premium Keeps Shrinking as the Nation Catches Up
paragraphs: Self-service Metano held flat at €1.966/L on September 16, unchanged from the day before, but still 11.65% above the national self-service average of €1.7608/L — by a wide margin the largest gap of any fuel this region carries relative to the rest of Italy.

That gap, though, is closing fast. In the week of July 20, Trentino-Alto Adige's average Metano price of €1.7993/L sat 19.96% above the national average of €1.4999/L. By the week of September 14, the region's price had risen to €1.966/L (+9.3% over the nine weeks) while the national average surged to €1.7477/L (+16.5% over the same span) — nearly double the region's rate of increase. The result: the regional premium has narrowed from roughly 20% to about 12.5%, a relative drop of more than a third. Metano is the fastest-moving fuel nationally this quarter by a wide margin, and Trentino-Alto Adige's historic status as an expensive outlier for natural gas is measurably eroding as the rest of the country's methane prices rush to catch up.

network_section.heading: A High-Reporting Region: 372 of 392 Stations Checked In Today
paragraphs: Trentino-Alto Adige has 392 registered fuel stations, of which 372 reported prices on September 16 — a 94.9% reporting rate, one station higher than the 371 that reported the day before. That compares favorably to the national reporting rate of 90.2% (21,645 of 24,000 registered stations), making this one of the more reliably-covered regions in the dataset on any given day.

A high and stable reporting rate matters for how much weight to put on the region's daily figures: with roughly 95% of registered stations checking in consistently, the daily and weekly averages presented here are unlikely to be skewed by a handful of stragglers dropping in and out of the sample, unlike lower-reporting regions where day-to-day swings can partly reflect which stations happened to report rather than genuine price movement.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made: No Spreadsheet, No Analyst, No Manual Step
paragraphs: Every part of this report — pulling the day's price and registry data, computing the weekly regional and national trend series, rotating deterministically through Italy's 20 regions by calendar date, and writing the analysis above in plain English — runs automatically, once a day, without a person opening a spreadsheet or copying a number by hand. The pipeline is built entirely with Claude Code: an AI coding agent wrote the scripts that fetch and reconcile the MIMIT price feeds, wrote the region-selection logic that guarantees every region gets its turn on a fixed cycle, and generates this narrative fresh each day directly from that day's real figures.

Contrast that with the standard way this kind of tracking usually gets built: someone maintains a spreadsheet, manually pastes in new numbers, and writes up a summary if and when they have time — a process that decays the moment that person is busy, on leave, or moves on. This report and the live dashboard behind it are proof that the same job — ingesting messy public data, computing real trends, and communicating them clearly — can be handled end-to-end by an unattended, self-updating system, with a human only in the loop to review before anything gets shared publicly.

closing.heading: Explore Further on the Live Dashboard
paragraphs: The live Fuel Dashboard at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/ opens by default on Agip Eni's brand-level view, but that's just the starting point — use the scope picker to switch to Region, Province, Municipality, or any other Operator/Brand to dig into the numbers that matter most to you, whether that's your own province's diesel prices or how a specific chain compares to the market nationally.

pull_quote: Trentino-Alto Adige's methane premium over the rest of Italy has narrowed from nearly 20% to about 12.5% since late July — not because local prices fell, but because the national average is catching up nearly twice as fast.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight lands on Trentino-Alto Adige, and the standout finding isn't the daily price — it's a nine-week trend. The region has long carried Italy's steepest premium on Metano (natural gas for vehicles), but that gap has shrunk from roughly 20% to about 12.5% since late July, simply because national methane prices are rising almost twice as fast as the region's own. Petrol and diesel, meanwhile, are moving in near-lockstep with the national market, and LPG is one of the only fuels bucking the trend by rising locally while easing nationally.

Fuel Dashboard tracks self-service and served prices for Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano across every Italian region, province, municipality and fuel brand, updated daily from Italy's official MIMIT price feed. You can explore it yourself at https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/.

What I think is worth calling out: this entire dashboard, the daily data pipeline, the regional rotation logic, and even the ~10-page report this caption comes from are built and run end-to-end with Claude Code, an AI coding agent. No spreadsheet, no manual data entry, no analyst writing a weekly summary by hand — just code that pulls the data, computes the trends, and writes the analysis, every single day. It's a small but concrete example of what's now possible when you use AI tools to build infrastructure instead of maintaining it manually: a self-updating dashboard and report that would otherwise take a person real recurring time to produce, running unattended.
